title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua sign contracts for 2026 fight
content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have both signed contracts to finally fight each other late in 2026.

The two former world heavyweight champions have agreed the details for a bout which will be broadcast live on streaming giant Netflix.

No specific date or venue has been confirmed yet but the particulars of each fighter’s contract have now been agreed.

Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Al-Sheikh has led negotiations and the fight is expected to be a Ring Magazine event, although the specific promoter will depend on the location of the fight.

Al-Sheikh posted on X: “To my friends in Great Britain – it’s happening. It’s signed.” Matchroom Promotions chairman Eddie Hearn, Joshua’s promoter, posted on Instagram: “Signed, sealed, delivered! AJ v Fury is on!”

Joshua, 36, will first face little-known Albanian Kristian Prenga in a bout on July 25 in Saudi Arabia as part of a “multi-fight deal” and that will be broadcast on DAZN.

It will be the British heavyweight’s first outing since he beat Jake Paul in December but was then involved in a serious car accident while in Nigeria. Joshua’s two close friends, Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele, were killed in the motor vehicle collision but the boxer escaped without any serious injury.

Joshua’s team were insistent in negotiations for the Fury bout that he would have a warm-up bout first due to him getting back to full fitness following the accident.

Joshua said: “It’s no secret I’ve taken some time to consolidate and rebuild to be ready for stepping back into the ring and today is the next step on that journey. I’m delighted to have agreed a multi-fight deal starting with July 25th in the kingdom of Saudi Arabia.”

The Fury bout will be dependent on Joshua coming through the Prenga fight unscathed, although given the Albanian’s limited record that is not expected to be a problem.

Fury, 37, was close to signing a contract to face Joshua in 2021 before Deontay Wilder won an arbitration hearing with U.S. judge to confirm his deal for a third fight with the British heavyweight had no expired.

Joshua went on to face Oleksandr Usyk and lost back-to-back bouts in 2021 and 2022 with the Ukrainian before suffering another loss at the hands of Daniel Dubois in 2024.

Fury also lost twice to Usyk in 2024 but returned with a win earlier this month when he beat Arslanbek Makhmudov.

London’s Wembley Stadium and Dublin’s Croke Park are both under consideration for the bout but other venues are also being looked at.

There is no doubt that this fight is too late in both men’s respective careers. They’re now at a combined age of 73 and by the time they finally fight – if everything goes to plan – they will also be a year older each.

That’s not to say it won’t be a big event. It will be a huge draw on both the live gate and on Netflix given the star status of both men, particularly in the UK.

The build-up will also be exciting and entertaining given their rivalry. However, it is no longer the best fight to be made in boxing nor will it be deciding who the top heavyweight is of this era.

When it was last close to happening in 2021, it would have been both. Fury held the WBC title and was unbeaten while Joshua had the three other belts – WBA, IBF and WBO – and had avenged the only blemish on his record at the time which was Andy Ruiz Jr.

Then came along Usyk and he beat both men twice to cement himself as the best heavyweight of this era and pushed both Fury and Joshua down the pecking order.

We’ve also been here before – with claims that it is on. There are agreements in place but until we have a date and venue confirmed then there will remain doubts it ever happens.
